lines.text: Saul keeps two thousand men at Michmash while Jonathan leads a thousand at Hebron and attacks the Philistine outpost at Geba.
The people gather to Saul at Gilgal, and when the Philistines camp at Michmash, the men of Israel hide in caves.
After Saul waits seven days for Samuel and his troops begin to desert, he offers the burnt offering.
Samuel tells Saul his kingdom will not endure, then goes up to Gibeah, and Saul counts about two thousand men.
Philistine raiders go out in three divisions, and on the day of battle only Saul and Jonathan have swords or spears.
